mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS), or the rate remains below 5.25% for the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL monthly inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, investors anticipate a protracted inflationary period, prompting a flight to quality and a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the next 20 days, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly different from the mean of the prior 30 months when CPIAUCSL > 3% for 2 months (one-tailed t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment) signals a strengthening labor market, which amplifies optimism and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 20,000 jobs while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: The 5-day SPX forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when the PAYEMS/UNRATE interaction meets the specified trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in GDPC1 (real personal consumption) of at least 2% for two consecutive months predicts a temporary boost in equity valuations as investors anticipate continued consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by at least 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns show no correlation with GDPC1 growth (R-squared < 0.05) during the triggered period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) of more than 5% in a month coincides with a decline in investor confidence, producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as expectations of future economic weakness rise.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 5% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 60 days following the trigger, SPX 60-day returns are not statistically different from the mean of the prior 12 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for three consecutive months, the expectation of continued monetary easing supports risk appetite, resulting in positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the accommodation phase (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3.5% while HOUST (housing starts) remains flat for two months indicates a labor market softening, which can lead to increased bearish positioning and negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% while HOUST is unchanged for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: The 5-day SPX forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when the UNRATE/HOUST interaction triggers.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in RSAFS (retail sales) of more than 10% in two consecutive months followed by a sustained decline in PAYEMS (employment growth) suggests a supply-side shock, which can depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by > 10% in two consecutive months then PAYEMS decreases for the next 2 months
regime_hint: retail sales surge followed by labor weakness
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the combined RSAFS/PAYEMS pattern.
